title: 'Unprofessional': Sanjay Manjrekar slams Sri Lanka’s antics in Colombo
content: Sanjay Manjrekar expressed disappointment with Sri Lanka's conduct as the match neared its climax, deeming their reaction to the fading light as somewhat unprofessional and distracting. While India declared their first innings, Sri Lanka stumbled to 8/2. In contrast, Manjrekar commended India's determination to continue playing despite the rain, highlighting their dominant position going into the next phase of the game.

title: US proposes higher H-1B visa filing fees: What companies may pay
content: The Department of Homeland Security has announced a proposal for a new fee of $103,265 for H-1B visa petitions, aimed at funding immigration system costs across various agencies. This fee specifically targets cap-subject applications, saving universities and research institutions from its impact. Notably, it is distinct from a previously invalidated proclamation payment. Currently, public commentary on this proposal is being encouraged.

title: ‘Swimming pool at Talkatora Stadium’: AAP mocks BJP over waterlogging at Nabin event
content: The Aam Aadmi Party criticized the Bharatiya Janata Party after waterlogging occurred at Talkatora Stadium. BJP leaders had gathered there to flag off "Pavan Mati Kalash" processions for Sant Ravidas' birth anniversary. AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar shared a video showing the event amidst flooded stadium grounds. He sarcastically congratulated Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta for the arrangements. The BJP stated the campaign aims to spread Sant Ravidas' teachings across society.

title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan’s $125m school to shut after 10 yrs
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution for low-income families, has closed its doors after a decade. Funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ceased, prompting the board's unanimous decision to shut down. While offering extensive support services, the school's academic results did not meet state benchmarks. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative is providing financial support for the transition and educational savings accounts.

title: Watch: Man fined Rs 5,500 after girlfriend covers his car with 3,400 lipstick kisses
content: A Gwalior resident faced a fine after his car was covered in lipstick marks. His girlfriend applied thousands of kiss imprints, transforming the vehicle into a canvas. Traffic police identified the car from social media images and traced its owner. The extensive exterior modification violated vehicle appearance and road safety regulations. The car owner paid the fine and had the lipstick marks removed from his vehicle.

title: Meet Leon Wang, teen who found 2 drugs that may reduce Alzheimer's damage
content: A young student's research explored existing medicines for Alzheimer's disease protection.  He identified two drugs, nintedanib and pirfenidone, showing protective effects in cell models.  This drug repurposing approach offers a faster, less expensive research starting point.  Wang's work highlights targeting APOE4 and brain blood vessel cell changes.  His findings suggest further investigation into TGFβ pathway drugs is warranted.

title: Amazon & Flipkart’s new cancellation fees has made sellers unhappy
content: Amazon and Flipkart have changed seller cancellation fees ahead of the festive season. Flipkart introduced a three-tier penalty structure for order fulfilment lapses. Amazon is also increasing closing fees across its fulfillment channels. Sellers express concern over increased financial burdens and thin operating margins. These changes aim to improve planning and customer experience for online marketplaces.

title: 'Horrifying to the core': Gurgaon rain traps kids in school buses for over 7 hours
content: A severe monsoon downpour caused extensive flooding across Gurgaon roads on Monday. Many school buses were stranded for several hours, causing significant distress to students. Parents faced helplessness while tracking their children and exchanging updates on messaging groups. Some parents waded through deep water to reach their children from stranded buses. The incident highlighted the city's recurring infrastructure failures during heavy rainfall.

title: 'State tried to airbrush Imran Khan out': Atherton on appeal for ex-Pakistan PM
content: In a compelling show of solidarity, Michael Atherton, the former England cricket captain, along with 21 fellow international cricketers, has launched an appeal for the medical treatment of ex-Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan, who is currently imprisoned. Atherton raised alarms about the efforts to diminish Khan's status, while Kapil Dev advocated for the essential rights of prisoners, urging for adequate healthcare and dignity without interfering in judicial processes.

title: Video shows Dumri MLA Jairam Mahto allegedly abusing cop on call, FIR filed
content: A purported video of MLA Jairam Mahto using abusive language has gone viral. The incident reportedly followed a dispute and escalated at the police station. Police sources claim the conversation was recorded by the station officer. An FIR has been registered against the MLA and nine others. The police are yet to confirm the video's authenticity.

title: Rare amoeba infection death: 8-yr-old girl dies after lake swim in Louisiana
content: In a shocking turn of events, an eight-year-old girl succumbed to a rare brain-eating amoeba after swimming in a Louisiana lake. This terrifying infection, typically fatal, remains exceedingly rare with minimal reported cases by the CDC. To help reduce the chances of such infections, health authorities advise keeping water out of the nose while swimming.

title: CCTV shows BJP MLA's daughter slapping cop at Karnataka temple
content: CCTV footage shows an altercation between an MLA's daughter and a police sub-inspector. The incident occurred at a temple during celebrations and involved a dispute over temple entry. The daughter allegedly slapped the officer, who then retaliated, leading to intervention by others. Police registered an FIR against the daughter for assaulting a public servant. The MLA apologized for his daughter's conduct and called for a departmental inquiry.

title: ‘Constitutional monstrosity’: P Chidambaram attacks One Nation, One Election Bill
content: Senior Congress leader P Chidambaram argued against simultaneous elections in 2029. He stated the proposed legislation violates constitutional basics and federal democracy principles. Chidambaram believes the bill's text prevents elections in 2029, which he sees as fortunate. The parliamentary committee received suggestions to define grounds for deferring state polls. Opposition parties plan a nationwide campaign against the "constitutional monstrosity" legislation.

title: RBI intervenes to support rupee as oil prices, dollar demand rise: Report
content: The Reserve Bank of India likely intervened in foreign exchange markets. Elevated oil prices and corporate dollar demand pressured the rupee. State-run banks offered dollars, indicating central bank action. The rupee remained range-bound for two weeks due to sustained intervention. Geopolitical tensions and equity market weakness also impacted the currency.

title: Who was Alyshia Rushing? 'Mama A' dies at 26 in Alabama car crash
content: Alyshia Rushing, known as TikTok’s “Mama A,” died at 26 after a two-vehicle crash in Montgomery, Alabama, on August 22. Police are investigating the crash, which also killed Landon Dunn. Rushing leaves four children, and a GoFundMe has been launched to support them and their father with daily needs, schooling, housing, childcare and counseling.

title: 'What do you think of yourself?': Ex-Pak cricketer responds to ‘worst team’ tag
content: Salman Butt defended Pakistan's cricket team against harsh British media criticism. He argued the team never claimed to be world champions or a dominant force. Butt highlighted England's diverse player origins while defending Pakistan's homegrown talent. England secured a significant innings victory over Pakistan in the first Test. This defeat marked a new era for the English team after coaching changes.

title: Roger Federer comeback? Tennis legend rules out return like Serena Williams
content: In New York for an exhibition match during the excitement of US Open Fan Week, Roger Federer confirmed he has no aspirations to return to competitive tennis. Following his retirement in September 2022, he has relished his time away from the court, focusing on family and personal training. The legendary player is also poised to be honored with an induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame soon.

title: 'Not integral to Islam': HC junks UP girl's plea for allowing hijab in school
content: Allahabad High Court dismissed a student's plea for wearing a headscarf with her uniform.  The court found no evidence that headscarves are an essential religious practice in Islam.  Photographs showed no other students, even from the same community, wore headscarves.  The bench noted a lack of factual foundation to support the claim of religious necessity.  Previous High Court opinions also stated headscarves are not integral to Islam.

title: Doctor reveals kidney disease symptoms that have nothing to do with your kidneys
content: Kidney disease can silently escalate, often going unnoticed until it's quite advanced. However, straightforward blood and urine tests can reveal early signs of kidney problems before any serious damage happens. Symptoms such as swelling, fatigue, or modifications in urination might hint at issues. Furthermore, high blood pressure plays a critical role in kidney health, making regular monitoring essential.

title: Dera chief Ram Rahim walks out of jail again, gets 21-day furlough in 17th release
content: Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh has received another 21-day parole from jail.  He is currently serving a 20-year sentence for rape convictions.  This marks his seventeenth parole release since 2020.  Prison rules allow convicts up to ten weeks of parole annually.  His repeated releases have drawn significant public scrutiny and attention.

title: SUV on rampage kills 71-year-old woman in Delhi; hits several vehicles
content: Tragedy struck near Kailash Colony metro station when an SUV, driven by Tapan Ahir, collided with several vehicles before hitting an elderly couple. Shashi Bhateja, 71, tragically lost her life at Moolchand Hospital, while her husband suffered a fracture and serious eye injuries. The driver was apprehended at the scene for further investigation.

title: ‘Demands unmet’: CJP calls march on Sept 5
content: The Cockroach Janta Party is set to stage a peaceful march to the Delhi Police headquarters, urging the government to uphold its promises made to youth who are protesting. Families of NEET students who tragically lost their lives will spearhead this demonstration, joined by survivors and fellow students.

title: Ex-Australia star picks 'perfect' coach for Chennai Super Kings
content: Stephen Fleming had been in charge of CSK for close to 16 years and guided the franchise to five IPL titles and two Champions League crowns. However, after a couple of disappointing seasons, Fleming stepped down. Hayden described the decision as a bold one while praising the partnership between Fleming and MS Dhoni.

title: Heavy rain lashes Delhi-NCR; Gurgaon offices, schools shift to online mode
content: Heavy rains continued to lash Delhi-NCR on Tuesday after Monday's downpour.  Authorities directed corporate offices and schools to adopt work-from-home and remote learning.  Widespread waterlogging and traffic snarls significantly disrupted daily life across the capital.  Civic agencies focused on drainage clearing and urgent road restoration work.  Residents faced similar flooding situations just weeks earlier.

title: Rupee slips to 95.74 against US dollar as crude prices, importer demand weigh
content: On Tuesday, the Indian Rupee faced a minor decline against the US dollar, influenced by rising crude oil prices and increased demand from importers. The Reserve Bank of India stepped in to stabilize the currency, keeping its fluctuations minimal. Meanwhile, domestic equities opened softly, although foreign institutional investors maintained their purchasing momentum in the stock market.

title: Karnataka suspends Amazon, Instamart, BigBasket licences over 'datura' sale
content: Karnataka authorities suspended food licences for Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, and BigBasket.  Toxic datura fruits and seeds were found sold as food products on these platforms.  The department ordered immediate removal of all datura listings and advertisements.  Selling and distributing datura as food poses a serious public health risk.  Consumption of unpurified datura can lead to coma and death in extreme cases.

title: Mumbai only Indian city in global Work From Anywhere Index, ahead of London, Miami
content: Mumbai has emerged as a prime hub for remote professionals, owing to its competitive transport costs and abundant flexible workspace options. As India's flexible workspace market expands rapidly, this city leads in Asia. The increasing adoption of Work From Anywhere policies has inspired many to combine travel with work, resulting in longer vacations to accommodate remote tasks.

title: In 1981, Sudha Murty lent Rs 10,000 to start Infosys: Their enduring bond
content: The bond between N. R. Narayana Murthy and Sudha Murty originated from their shared love of literature, evolving into a remarkable alliance. Sudha's investment of ₹10,000 was crucial for the inception of Infosys, even though her non-founding status once left her feeling undervalued. Despite their individual journeys, they fostered a robust partnership grounded in trust and admiration.

title: ‘Hire and train Americans’: JD Vance defends proposed six-figure H-1B fee
content: The US Department of Homeland Security proposed a new $103,265 fee for H-1B visa petitions. This fee aims to recover government costs for administering the immigration system. Vice President JD Vance supports the proposal, emphasizing hiring American workers. Indian professionals, a major beneficiary group, could be significantly impacted by this change. The public has thirty days to submit comments on this proposed rule.

Both players faced fines and demerit points from the ICC as a consequence. Pujara and Raman highlighted the impact of Jaiswal's frustration on the incident, while Karim emphasized the importance of setting a positive example for young cricket enthusiasts.

content: Danielle Belluomini, wife of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York, has largely maintained a private life despite her husband’s high-profile NFL career. A former sixth-grade science teacher, she married York in 2011, and they share two sons, Jaxon and Brixton. Belluomini has made occasional appearances at NFL events but largely avoids the spotlight. Their marriage drew renewed attention after York filed for divorce in May 2026, months before his Ohio arrest.

The rising valuation highlights the couple’s growing influence in women’s sports and comes as Patrick continues his recovery while preparing for his NFL return.
